title: Doctors Concerned about Return of Iodine Deficiency
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: A century ago, iodine deficiency affected children across much of the United States.
sentences.zh: 一个世纪前,缺碘影响到美国大部分地区的儿童。

sentences.en: The problem mostly disappeared during the 1900s after iodine was added to common foods.
sentences.zh: 在1900年代,在将碘添加到普通食品之后,这个问题大多消失了。

sentences.en: But doctors are now seeing higher iodine deficiency rates.
sentences.zh: 但医生现在发现缺碘率较高。

sentences.en: The rises are blamed on dietary changes and new food manufacturing methods.
sentences.zh: 由于饮食变化和新的食品制造方法,导致产量上升。

sentences.en: What is iodine? Iodine is an element found in seawater and in some soils — mostly in coastal areas.
sentences.zh: 碘是什么?碘是海水和一些土壤——主要是沿海地区——中的一种成分。

sentences.en: A French chemist accidentally discovered the substance in 1811.
sentences.zh: 一名法国化学家于1811年意外发现了该物质。

sentences.en: Iodine’s name comes from a Greek word meaning violet-colored.
sentences.zh: 爱奥丁的名字来自希腊语,

sentences.en: Later in the 1800s, scientists began to understand that people need iodine to control their metabolism and stay healthy.
sentences.zh: 1800年代后期 科学家们开始认识到 人们需要碘来控制他们的新陈代谢 保持健康

sentences.en: The element is also important for a child’s brain development.
sentences.zh: 这个元素对于儿童的大脑发育也很重要。

sentences.en: One sign of iodine deficiency is an increase in size, or swelling, of the neck.
sentences.zh: 缺碘的一个迹象是颈部大小增加或肿胀。

sentences.en: This growth in the neck is known as a goiter.
sentences.zh: 颈部的这种增长被称为甲状腺肿。

sentences.en: It can appear when the thyroid gland grows to make up for too little iodine to produce hormones that control certain body processes.
sentences.zh: 当甲状腺生长 弥补少碘 产生荷尔蒙 以控制某些身体过程时 就会出现

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, goiters were commonly seen in children in some parts of the United States.
sentences.zh: 1900年代初期,在美国一些地区,儿童中经常出现甲状腺肿。

sentences.en: Some of the children showed other symptoms in addition to goiters.
sentences.zh: 有些儿童除了甲状腺肿外,还表现出其他症状。

sentences.en: These included being smaller or experiencing deafness.
sentences.zh: 这些障碍包括体积较小或聋哑。

sentences.en: Adding iodine to salt In the past, public health experts realized they could not solve the iodine deficiency problem by feeding everyone seaweed and seafood.
sentences.zh: 过去,公共卫生专家认识到他们无法通过喂养每个人的海藻和海鲜来解决缺碘问题。

sentences.en: But they learned iodine can be included with table salt.
sentences.zh: 但他们学会了碘可以加食盐。

sentences.en: This form of salt, known as iodized salt, first became available in 1924.
sentences.zh: 这种被称为加碘盐的盐,最早于1924年供应。

sentences.en: By the 1950s, more than 70 percent of U.S. households used iodized table salt.
sentences.zh: 到1950年代,70%以上的美国家庭使用加碘食盐。

sentences.en: Bread and some other foods also had iodine.
sentences.zh: 面包和其他一些食物也有碘。

sentences.en: As a result, iodine deficiency in the U.S. became rare.
sentences.zh: 因此,美国碘缺乏症变得罕见。

sentences.en: But diets have changed over the years. Processed foods now make up a large part of the American diet.
sentences.zh: 但多年来,饮食已经改变。 加工食品现在构成美国饮食的一大部分。

sentences.en: Although these foods contain a lot of salt, it is not iodized.
sentences.zh: 虽然这些食物含有大量盐,但并未加碘。

sentences.en: Leading bread makers also no longer add iodine.
sentences.zh: 主要面包制造商也不再添加碘。

sentences.en: And for people who do salt their food, it is popular now to use kosher salt, Himalayan rock salt or other products that do not contain iodine.
sentences.zh: 对于食用盐的人来说 食用磷酸盐 喜马拉雅岩石盐 或其他不含碘的产品是流行的

sentences.en: “People have forgotten why there’s iodine in salt,” said Dr.
sentences.zh: “人们已经忘记了为什么盐里有碘,”

sentences.en: Elizabeth Pearce of Boston Medical Center.
sentences.zh: 波士顿医疗中心的伊丽莎白·皮尔斯

sentences.en: She is a leader in the Iodine Global Network, a nongovernmental agency working to end conditions linked to iodine deficiency .
sentences.zh: 她是Iodine全球网络的领导者,

sentences.en: Pearce noted there had been a reported 50 percent drop in U.S. iodine levels studied during the 1970s through the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 皮尔斯注意到,据报告,1970年代至1990年代,美国研究的碘含量下降了50%。

sentences.en: How much iodine is enough? While most Americans are getting enough iodine through diet, doctors worry this is not the case for women and children – the two groups most likely to be hurt by iodine deficiency.
sentences.zh: 多少碘足够? 虽然大多数美国人通过饮食获得足够的碘,但医生担心妇女和儿童的情况并非如此 — — 这两个群体最有可能因缺碘而受伤。

sentences.en: The American Academy of Pediatrics and other medical groups advise that all pregnant and breastfeeding women get 150 micrograms of iodine each day.
sentences.zh: 美国儿科学会和其他医疗团体建议,所有孕妇和哺乳期妇女每天获得150微克碘。

sentences.en: In the last 15 years or so, U.S. researchers have increasingly reported seeing mild iodine deficiency in pregnant women.
sentences.zh: 在过去15年左右的时间里,美国研究人员越来越多地报告孕妇患有轻微缺碘症。

sentences.en: A Michigan State University study of about 460 pregnant women found about 25 percent of them were not getting enough.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州立大学对大约460名孕妇的研究发现,其中约25%的孕妇得不到足够的营养。

sentences.en: That study’s lead writer, Jean Kerver, noted that many vitamins for pregnant women do not contain iodine.
sentences.zh: 该研究的主要作者Jean Kerver指出,许多孕妇的维生素不含碘。

sentences.en: As a result, doctors suggest that pregnant or breastfeeding women check labels to make sure the vitamins or supplements they take have iodine.
sentences.zh: 因此,医生建议孕妇或哺乳期妇女检查标签,以确保她们服用的维生素或补充剂有碘。

sentences.en: Some studies have linked even mild iodine deficiency to a lower score on an intelligence test known as an intelligence quotient (IQ) test.
sentences.zh: 一些研究甚至将轻微缺碘与被称为智商测试的情报测试分数较低联系起来。

sentences.en: But experts say there has not yet been enough research to establish exactly how the U.S. population is being affected by iodine deficiency.
sentences.zh: 但专家说,还没有开展足够的研究,以确定美国人口是如何受到缺碘影响的。

sentences.en: Dr. Monica Serrano-Gonzalez of Brown University said she and other doctors had seen five cases of iodine deficiency in children visiting a local health center in Providence, Rhode Island. “We’re concerned this may be increasing, especially in patients with restricted diets.”
sentences.zh: 布朗大学的Monica Serrano-Gonzalez博士说,她和其他医生在罗得岛普罗维登斯的一个地方保健中心看到五例儿童缺碘病例。 “我们担心这种情况可能正在增加,特别是在饮食受限的病人中。 ”

sentences.en: Serrano-Gonzalez called for increasing publicity about the problem in order to prevent it from getting worse.
sentences.zh: Serrano-Gonzalez呼吁增加对这一问题的宣传,以防止问题恶化。

sentences.en: She said, “This needs to be on people’s radar.” I’m John Russell.
sentences.zh: 她说 : “ 这需要人们的注意。 ”我是约翰·罗素。

sentences.en: Mike Stobbe reported on this story for the Associated Press.
sentences.zh: Mike Stobbe为美联社报导了这个故事。

sentences.en: John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: John Russell改编了它 用于VOA学习英语。
